answer: Tarvik High (design target; the golden's wording is fixed at ship from the generator)
answer_source: the design note's Ladder; at ship task181/golden/, written by the generator from target/ and recomputed by the verifier

spine.entity: one flight's traversal of one elementary en-route sector (entry and exit time and flight level, as the flight data processing system logged it)

world.geography: fictional country (Aldmark), northern Europe, EUR ICAO region
world.org_type: national air navigation service provider's area control centre with eight elementary en-route sectors

driver: Events arise when one moving unit passes through the position of another present at the same time, so the expected count follows the crossings a period's traffic creates rather than the time units spend, their number or its square; a forward change that sends new units across a dense existing flow multiplies the crossings while barely adding time, so scaling last period's events by time spent, by counts, by their square or by the time spent changing position keeps a unit under a rate limit that its crossings carry over it.
driver_concrete: Losses of separation in the Holmvik centre happen where one aircraft climbs or descends through the level of another in the same sector, so each sector's summer 2027 losses follow the vertical crossings in the 2027 traffic sample; Brekka's new base sends about thirty departures a day climbing through Tarvik High's eastbound cruise levels, adding about 2 per cent to its flight hours and roughly doubling its crossings, which takes it over the safety plan's 12.0 losses per 100,000 flight hours while every other sector stays under.
stump: A competent solver keeps each sector's summer 2026 losses of separation per 100,000 flight hours, scales each sector's losses with its 2027 flight hours from the traffic sample and files that no sector reaches the safety plan's 12.0 in summer 2027 (Mosby High highest at about 11); the step that lands it there is forecasting losses from flight hours when separation is lost where one aircraft climbs or descends through another's level, so the Brekka departures that add about 2 per cent to Tarvik High's flight hours roughly double its vertical crossings and take it to about 14.5.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who deduplicates the occurrence records, keeps the ATM-related losses of separation, attributes each to its elementary sector under the night configurations and computes summer flight hours exactly still forecasts summer 2027 by scaling each sector's losses with its flight hours, with the square of its traffic or with its climbing and descending flight hours, and files that no sector exceeds 12.0, because only counting the vertical crossings in each sector shows the new Brekka departures taking Tarvik High over the tolerance.
domain_test: What decides the call is air traffic control's human-factors safety analysis of controller workload: a loss of separation is a controller error in a vertical interaction (one aircraft cleared through the level of another), so a sector's expected losses follow the vertical crossings in its traffic, a complexity measure the field uses beside flight hours; with another field's nouns there are no flight levels to cross and no climb through a cruising flow, so the task does not survive the swap.

differentiation.task229: task229 v1 builds a standard error over shared parent nodes (entities that fail together); task181 v4 builds the exposure unit as a vertical crossing between two aircraft in one sector, and its forecast follows the crossings, never an error term.
differentiation.task98: task98 v3 forms each unit by chaining members within a distance under a per-unit threshold; task181 v4 forms no group: the exposure is each pair where one aircraft changes level through another's, and the forward change is new traffic multiplying those pairs.
differentiation.task60: task60 v8 counts people filed by two filers once under a tie-break; task181 v4 counts encounters between two aircraft (vertical crossings), and the forward count scales with those pairs rather than with flight hours or with any roll of units.

lineage.driver: Exposure to a compromised device happens only on the channels that pass a unit's data through that device, so a common-source screen that counts every visit at the site grain dilutes one compromised device among the site's untouched channels.

lineage.fate: spent at in-house solver round 1 (2026-10-11): one solver, proxy 94.5, landed 387 by explaining the co-visited plaza sites away as subsets of the pump's victims and re-screening the residual; any further rung is dismissed by the same subset check or opens a fork
lineage.driver: Victims of two independent sources are pooled, so the dominant source's victims make the places they also passed look like sources and pull the second source down among ordinary places; only attributing victims to the strongest source first and screening the victims it leaves unexplained separates the second source from the co-visited places, and the exposed population is the union of both sources' exposures.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-11: missed at in-house rounds 2 and 3 only while the estimand was open; the portal's determinism QC called the cases-on-file against eventual-count reading a fork, and once PR-07 4.2 filed the eventual count literally, round 4 landed (96.8) by completing each case on its own laboratory's delay; hardening loop 1 (a dated change in the slow laboratory's process) found that any filed criterion choosing the delay history names the step, so the architecture cannot be both literally deterministic and stumped; re-rooted to architecture 3
lineage.driver: When a count is read before its records have finished arriving, the units whose records arrive slowest look quiet exactly while they are surging, so the comparison has to be made on the complete count each unit's own arrival history implies, not on what has arrived, and not on an arrival speed pooled across units.

lineage.architecture: v3 (a housing association's community safety log: which estate's winter target-hardening grant, near-repeat burglary runs against each estate's background rate)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-11 at design, never built: the filed back-test that had to select the background projection does not select it on honest data (about ten break-ins per estate-quarter; the usual winter wins the back-test in most seeds, the golden cell in 8 per cent), so no criterion, window or volume closes the method without planting
lineage.driver: When events arrive both from a steady background and in short self-exciting runs, each run a burst of events close in place and time that ends once it has played out, a unit's recent count overstates its coming count exactly where a run has just passed, so the coming count follows the unit's background rate, which only separating the run events (each within a short distance and interval of an earlier one) from the rest recovers; projecting whole counts by any persistence, seasonal or smoothing rule names a unit whose run is over instead of the unit whose background has risen.
